protocol.py: VERIFIED against plate map dil-03. 8 of 8 wells hold what the plate map says.
  Destination: NEST 96 Well Plate 200 µL Flat (slot 4). Reading of the request: 8 standards;
    excess removed from the last well.

Labware for the technique (Serial dilution): nothing to flag.

Where every liquid ended up (ul):
  liquid                             declared delivered in source elsewhere    lost
  bsa                                  1000.0      99.6     900.0       0.4     0.0
  water                                1000.0     300.4     650.0      49.6     0.0
  Note: bsa ends in wells the plate map does not list for it: A1 in slot 5 (0.4 ul).
  Note: water ends in wells the plate map does not list for it: A1 in slot 5 (49.6 ul).

Prep sheet: what to put on the deck before the run.
  slot labware                               well  liquid                       load at least  declared
  2    Opentrons 15 Tube Rack with Falcon 15 A1    bsa                                  100.0    1000.0
  3    NEST 12 Well Reservoir 15 mL          A1    water                                350.0    1000.0
  Tips: 1 from Opentrons OT-2 96 Tip Rack 300 µL in slot 1.
  'Load at least' is what the robot draws. Add the dead volume of your tube or reservoir.

This checks the logic of the protocol: what goes where, and how much. It does not check the
  physics: whether a viscous liquid is pipetted accurately, or a drop stays on a tip.

check_text:
protocol.py: 4 biology problems (2 warnings, 2 notes).

1. WARNING CONTAM-STOCK: A used tip went into a stock: water (well A1 in slot 3)
   line 41:  p300.aspirate(add_diluent_vol, water_reservoir["A1"])
   At line 41 the tip went into water (well A1 in slot 3) while it still carried bsa (tube
   A1 in slot 2) from an earlier step. A tip that has touched one liquid leaves a little of
   it in the next liquid it touches, so this stock now holds material that does not belong
   there. The protocol drew from it again afterwards, but only into wells that were given
   that material on purpose anyway, so this run is not harmed. What is left in the stock is
   no longer clean for the next run.
   Affected: well A1 in slot 3.
   Fix: Pick up a fresh tip before line 41 goes into the stock. Or change the order: hand
   out the shared liquid first, while the tip is still clean, and add the other liquids
   afterwards with a fresh tip each.
   Source: Lab Manager: minimizing cross-contamination in automated liquid handling
           https://www.labmanager.com/minimizing-cross-contamination-in-automated-liquid-handling-workflows-35194
   Source: WHO: dos and don'ts for molecular testing
           https://www.who.int/teams/global-malaria-programme/case-management/diagnosis/nucleic-acid-amplification-based-diagnostics/dos-and-don-ts-for-molecular-testing
   [8ba9c438801e]

2. WARNING MIX-TOO-WEAK: Mixing too weak to stir 6 wells: 1 × 100 ul in 100 ul
   line 49:  p300.mix(volume=transfer_vol + add_diluent_vol)
   At line 49 the tip mixes wells A2, A3, A4, A5, A6 and A7 in slot 4 with 1 stroke of 100
   ul in a well holding 100 ul (this line did it 6 times). 1 stroke of 100 ul move 1 of the
   well in all; it takes about 2 wells' worth of strokes to mix (the mixing work). Fewer
   than 3 strokes do not mix a well. A stroke of the whole well draws air at the bottom and
   foams the liquid. Integra draws over 80% of the well five times; three mixes gave 11.8%
   CV where twenty gave 1.7%. What the well holds is not at the concentration you
   calculated, and in a dilution series every later step inherits the error.
   Affected: wells A2, A3, A4, A5, A6 and A7 in slot 4.
   Fix: Mix the well with about 80% of its volume (80 ul) at least 5 times: `mix(5, 80,
   well)`. A stroke of the whole well draws air; use no more than 90%.
   Source: Integra: how to perform serial dilutions
           https://www.integra-biosciences.com/global/en/applicationguide/master-art-pipetting-and-learn-how-perform-serial-dilutions-our-comprehensive-guide
   Source: Integra: three serial-dilution protocols (over 80% of the volume, five times)
           https://www.integra-biosciences.com/global/en/applications/3-simple-and-proven-automation-protocols-serial-dilutions-assist-plus-pipetting-robot
   Source: Beckman AMPure XP instructions (mix with a tip volume just below the well volume)
           https://research.fredhutch.org/content/dam/research/hahn/methods/Agencourt%20AMPure%20XP.pdf
   Source: Esca Automation: serial dilution, a classic technique
           https://escaautomation.substack.com/p/serial-dilution-a-classic-technique
   Source: labautomation.io 3654: how to mix a bacteria sample enough
           https://labautomation.io/t/how-to-mix-bacteria-sample-enough/3654
   Source: Artel: automated liquid handlers as sources of error
           https://www.bioprocessintl.com/assays/automated-liquid-handlers-as-sources-of-error
   [99f71df5c065]

3. NOTE CONTAM-WELL: A used tip carried water (well A1 in slot 3) into well A1 in slot 4 it
was never meant for
   line 45:  p300.aspirate(transfer_vol, source)
   At line 45 the tip touched the liquid in well A1 in slot 4 while it still carried water
   (well A1 in slot 3) from an earlier step. A tip that has touched one liquid leaves a
   little of it in the next liquid it touches. The protocol never transfers that liquid into
   this well on purpose, so it was not meant to be there. If the wells hold different
   samples, each now holds a little of another.
   Affected: well A1 in slot 4.
   Fix: Use a fresh tip for each well at line 45. If one tip must serve many wells, dispense
   from above the liquid (for example `well.top()`) so that the tip never touches what is
   already in the well.
   Source: Lab Manager: minimizing cross-contamination in automated liquid handling
           https://www.labmanager.com/minimizing-cross-contamination-in-automated-liquid-handling-workflows-35194
   [23901b2ec9b2]

4. NOTE NO-NEGATIVE-CONTROL: No blank on a dilution series: 8 wells of bsa
   line 46:  p300.dispense(transfer_vol, plate[well])
   At line 46 the robot starts a dilution series of bsa in NEST 96 Well Plate 200 µL Flat
   (slot 4): 8 wells at 8 concentrations, each level about 2 times weaker than the one
   before. No well on this plate holds water with no sample, so there is no blank: the curve
   has no zero to read against, and a signal from the diluent or the plastic cannot be told
   from the lowest point. Wells: wells A1, A2, A3, A4, A5, A6, A7 and A8 in slot 4.
   Affected: wells A1, A2, A3, A4, A5, A6, A7 and A8 in slot 4.
   Fix: Add a well of water alone, and tell the plate map where it is.
   Source: MIQE 2009: a no-template control on every plate is essential
           https://gene-quantification.com/miqe-bustin-et-al-clin-chem-2009.pdf
   Source: MIQE 2.0 (2025): the no-template and no-RT controls, still essential
           https://academic.oup.com/clinchem/article/71/6/634/8119148
   Source: Bustin 2025: MIQE compliance remains patchy
           https://www.ebi.ac.uk/europepmc/webservices/rest/PMC12154065/fullTextXML
   Source: Qiagen bench guide: PCR controls (no-template, no-RT, positive)
           https://www.qiagen.com/en-us/knowledge-and-support/knowledge-hub/bench-guide/pcr/reference-genes-and-controls/pcr-controls
   Source: Bio-Rad real-time PCR applications guide: controls in triplicate
           https://www.bio-rad.com/webroot/web/pdf/lsr/literature/Bulletin_5279.pdf
   Source: Thermo Maxima SYBR manual: the NTC contains all components except template DNA
           https://assets.fishersci.com/TFS-Assets/LSG/manuals/MAN0012933_Maxima_SYBR_Green_qPCR_Master_ROX_Sol__k0251_UG.pdf
   [cdef25e50c47]

The Opentrons simulator (8.8.2) passed this protocol with no error: it checks that the robot
can make the moves, not what they do to the liquids.
